articles.title: Can gzip be a language model?
articles.summary: A compressor such as gzip can be used to generate language models by predicting the probability of each word in a given text based on its context. This is achieved through the compression-prediction equivalence, where every prediction model is inherently a compressor and all compression algorithms are prediction models. The algorithm uses a sliding window of 32 KiB to find matches against the recent text in the window, encoding continuation that echoes something already in the window as a cheap back-reference instead of literal bytes. This allows for the generation of coherent text with high probability, making it possible to prime a model and generate language models such as tiny Shakespeare.

The first four bytes of every Java class file contain this value, which is used to identify likely class files from non-class files. The origin of this value is unclear, but it is believed to have been chosen for its uniqueness and ease of handling in 32-bit systems. The Java team may have been inspired by the idea of a coffee cup with a face, as the letters C-A-F-E-B-A-B-E are reminiscent of a coffee cup with a face.

This is because AI is not capable of providing context or perspective, leading to a sense of disconnection from the original work. The authors of these documents often become impatient with readers who are not engaged, and the writing can become repetitive and lacking in nuance. This can lead to a loss of trust and communication, as the reader is left wondering what the author is trying to convey.

articles.title: Transformers Explained Visually
articles.summary: The Transformer architecture has revolutionized the field of artificial intelligence, particularly in text-generative models, by enabling models to process entire sequences and capture long-range dependencies more effectively than previous architectures. This is achieved through the use of a self-attention mechanism, which allows tokens to communicate with each other, capturing contextual information and relationships between words. The Transformer architecture consists of three key components: an embedding layer that converts text into numerical vectors, a transformer block that processes and transforms the input data, and output probabilities that enable the model to make predictions about the next token in a sequence.

articles.title: Relation algebra is not relational algebra
articles.summary: Relation algebra is a CS concept that is equivalent to domain-independent relational calculus, a well-behaved fragment of first-order logic queries. It is also equivalent to FOL3, which restricts first-order logic to use at most three different variables. However, it can be extended to match the expressive power of FOL with a fork operator. This concept has been quietly finding applications in computer science, including the Alloy analyzer, a database system that uses it as "relational logic".
